sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Macomb County?
sections.html:
Macomb County does not send most tax bills itself. The city, township or village treasurer where the parcel sits bills and collects the first year of taxes, and the county treasurer takes over only after taxes go delinquent. Under MCL 211.44, the bill must show the property description, taxable value and the amount of tax, and failure to send or receive a bill does not excuse the tax.

The county is the third most populous in Michigan, with 881,217 residents counted in 2020, and it holds 27 cities, townships and villages on a land area of 479 square miles. Warren, Sterling Heights and St. Clair Shores are among the cities, and Armada, New Haven and Romeo are villages. Because each municipality bills separately, a seller in Roseville and a seller in Romeo deal with different treasurer offices for the same county.

The Macomb County Treasurer's Office, reached at 586-469-5190 or treasurer@macombgov.org from 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. on weekdays, handles delinquent taxes. Its website offers online payment of delinquent real and personal property tax by debit card or ACH only.

sections.h2: Who sets my assessment, and who hears an appeal?
sections.html:
Your city or township assessor sets the assessment. The county Equalization Department does not determine any individual property's assessment. Its job, set by Section 211.34 of the General Property Tax Act, is to run sales and appraisal studies by property class in each city and township so local assessments are fair across the county. The department's phone is 586-469-5260, open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

If you disagree with a value, start with the local board of review. MCL 211.30 sets the first meeting for the second Monday in March, with alternative start dates of the Tuesday or Wednesday after, and at least 12 hours of hearings that week. A nonresident can protest by letter, and a city or township may also let residents do so by letter if its governing body adopts that option.

Each person who protests must be notified in writing of the result by the first Monday in June, with information about the right to further appeal to the Michigan Tax Tribunal and the final date for that filing. Use the date printed on your own notice. A protest that misses the March session waits for the next March. The July or December board of review has a narrower role: it can correct a taxable value that was reset after an assumed transfer of ownership that did not happen.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the taxable value on a Macomb County home?
sections.html:
Michigan assesses property at 50% of true cash value, but the amount you are taxed on is the taxable value, which is capped. Under MCL 211.27a, the taxable value in any year is the lesser of the prior year's taxable value times the lesser of 1.05 or the inflation rate, plus additions, with the result capped at the current state equalized value.

A sale ends the cap. For the calendar year after a transfer of ownership, taxable value is reset to the state equalized value, then the cap applies again until the next transfer. That is why a long-held home in Macomb can show a taxable value far below half of its market price while the buyer's first full bill is higher. The buyer must tell the local assessor within 45 days of the transfer.

Some transfers are not counted as transfers of ownership:

  • Transfers between spouses and from a decedent to a surviving spouse.
  • Residential transfers to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild that are not used commercially after the transfer.
  • Transfers through foreclosure, until the lender resells.
  • Conveyances to a trust where the settlor or spouse is the sole present beneficiary.
  • Court-ordered transfers with no stated price.

sections.h2: What happens when Macomb County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become delinquent on March 1 of the following year and are payable to the County Treasurer, with a 4% administration fee and 1% interest added, then 1% per month. The county describes it as a three-year process. Taxes still unpaid as of March 31 in the third year of delinquency are foreclosed, and title vests in the Macomb County Treasurer.

Forfeiture comes after the first year. The county adds a minimum $175 title search fee plus recording fees, and the interest rate rises to 1.5% per month, applied back to the original delinquency date. Forfeiture is not foreclosure: the owner keeps the right to redeem until March 31 of the third year. After that foreclosure is final, and the property goes first to the State, then to the local unit, and then to public auction between the third Tuesday in July and the first Tuesday in November.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Macomb County house that owes back taxes?
sections.html:
Yes. Back taxes are cleared with the title company at closing. The delinquent amount must be paid off for a clean transfer, and a warranty deed needs a treasurer's certificate under MCL 211.135 showing that taxes were paid for the five years before the deed date. Ask the County Treasurer at 586-469-5190 for a payoff figure that includes fees and interest through the closing date.

Forfeiture gives an owner a year to act, but the notices keep coming. The county sends four first class mailings, two certified notices and three newspaper notices, and staff visit the property each September. Macomb's Treasurer will explain the process, set up a payment plan or refer you to assistance programs.

If a home is already foreclosed, the previous owner cannot get it back. For foreclosures since 2021, a former owner or other interested party can file for any excess proceeds left after an auction sale beyond the taxes owed. In the county's 2025 tax year timeline, the claim deadline is July 1, 2028 and the court motion deadline is May 15, 2029. A seller facing this should act before the final March 31 date.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply at closing on a Macomb County sale?
sections.html:
Michigan taxes are billed in a summer and a winter levy, and the law lets a collecting unit add up to a 1% administration fee on tax paid before February 15 and a 3% late penalty after February 14 if the governing body authorizes it. A deed in Macomb carries the usual recording fee and transfer tax from the register of deeds, covered on the county's register of deeds page.

At closing, the escrow agent prorates the current year's bill between buyer and seller by the closing date, and the county treasurer's payoff figure covers any delinquent years. If the house is held in a trust or came from an estate, check whether the earlier transfer was a transfer of ownership, because that determines whether the next bill resets.

For questions about exemptions or the principal residence rate, call the assessor in your own city or township. Each unit keeps its own roll, and the county cannot change one parcel's assessment.

faqs.q: When do Macomb County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Unpaid taxes become delinquent on March 1 of the year after they are assessed, and then they are payable to the Macomb County Treasurer. For 2025 taxes the county's timeline lists March 3, 2026, and adds a 4% administration fee and 1% interest.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Macomb County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the assessor for your city or township, not the county. The county Equalization Department at 586-469-5260 checks assessments across the county but does not set an individual property's value.

faqs.q: How long before Macomb County forecloses on unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: It takes about three years. Taxes unpaid as of March 31 in the third year of delinquency are foreclosed and title vests in the county treasurer.

faqs.q: Does a sale raise the property tax in Macomb County?
faqs.a: Yes, often. After a transfer of ownership, taxable value resets to the state equalized value in the next year, then rises under the cap until the next transfer.

faqs.q: Can I get money back after a Macomb County tax foreclosure auction?
faqs.a: Possibly. Those who held an interest at foreclosure can file to claim leftover proceeds from an auction above the taxes owed, by the July 1 date in the county's timeline, then file a circuit court motion by the May 15 date listed there.
